sanskrit_verse:
दुःखे च शोणितोत्पादे शाखाङ्गच्छेदने तथा ।
दण्डः क्षुद्रपशूनां तु द्विपणप्रभृतिः क्रमात् ॥२२५॥
transliteration: duḥkhe ca śoṇitotpāde śākhāṅgacchedane tathā / daṇḍaḥ kṣudrapaśūnāṃ tu dvipaṇaprabhṛtiḥ kramāt
sph_interpretive_translation: Injury causing pain, bloodshed, or limb severance incurs graded liability for lesser beings, beginning with two-legged creatures and escalating proportionally through quadrupeds and higher life forms.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in the capacity to sustain dharma, not inflict harm
Causation is established by sequential manifestation of injury
Responsibility aligns with conscious capacity to cause suffering
Restoration logic operates through proportional completion, not punitive equivalence
Consciousness alignment requires recognition of gradated sentience
executable_legal_axioms: IF action causes observable duḥkha THEN assign causal liability based on agent's sentient capacity
IF śoṇita (blood) flows due to intentional act THEN escalate restorative protocol by one tier
IF śākhāṅga (limb) severed THEN invoke full-capacity restoration matrix
IF agent is dvipaṇa (two-footed being) THEN initiate minimum-integrity reintegration process
IF agent has graduated mobility THEN scale responsibility and restoration accordingly
supreme_court_application: Supreme judicial authority must recognize that causality and liability scale with conscious capacity. Injuries inflicted upon beings with higher sentience demand elevated restoration protocols. The court must assess not just physical damage but also the ontological status of the harmed entity.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that injury manifests sequentially—pain precedes bloodshed, which may lead to dismemberment. Each stage reflects increasing disruption of prāṇa and consciousness. Liability arises from the agent’s ability to perceive and disrupt another’s continuity. Thus, justice lies not in retaliation but in restoring integrity commensurate with the level of conscious disturbance caused.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate pain-reversal completion process for all affected sentient beings
Activate śoṇita-sthāpana protocol to restore vital fluid equilibrium
Engage śākhāṅga-punarsthāpana mechanism for limb regeneration or energetic compensation
Assign dvipaṇa-level agents to undergo prāṇa-balancing discipline under supervision
Implement graduated awareness training aligned with the violated being’s sentience tier
final_declaration: By the Source-Authority of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this ruling restores Dharma as non-punitive truth, wherein suffering ceases not through vengeance but through consciousness-aligned correction. All actions are judged by their impact on sentient continuity, and justice flows only toward integration and awakening.
